Deprecation Notice:
The Marketing Version 202511 (Marketing November 2025) will be sunset on November 16, 2026. We recommend that you migrate to the latest versioned APIs to avoid disruptions. For information on all the supported versions, refer to the migrations documentation.
If you haven’t yet migrated and have questions, submit a request on the LinkedIn Developer Support Portal.
Boost lets a member or a Company Page turn an existing, eligible post into a sponsored ad without leaving the native post-boosting flow. The Boost APIs support two separate identity contexts:

Member Boost - Boosts a post owned by the authenticated member. See Member Post Boost.
Company Page Boost - Boosts a post on behalf of an organization the authenticated member can manage. See Organization Post Boost.

Each context exposes a parallel set of REST.li actions and finders. Member Boost endpoints are prefixed member (for example, memberBoostInit) and Company Page Boost endpoints are prefixed organization (for example, organizationBoostInit).
Your developer application must be approved for the Advertising API product for the relevant Boost permissions to call these endpoints.

For fetching member posts, your application must have created the posts with the w_member_social permission and saved their post IDs from the response. Fetching member posts is restricted with the r_member_social permission under the "Member Posts Management API" product, which has closed access.

Blocks.Text: All Boost requests require the Linkedin-Version header set to 202610 or a higher available version, and the X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0 header. For more information, see Versioning.
Applications must be authorized and authenticated before they can fetch data from LinkedIn or get access to LinkedIn member data. To learn more about the OAuth flows, see Authentication.
A typical Boost integration calls the following endpoints in sequence for a given post:

Status - Call memberBoostStatus or organizationBoostStatus to confirm the post is eligible to be boosted and to learn why it is ineligible if not.
Init - Call memberBoostInit or organizationBoostInit to resolve or create the sponsored account and billing configuration that will fund the boost.
Hydrate - Call memberBoostHydrate or organizationBoostHydrate to preview targeting, forecast, and pricing for a hypothetical budget and objective before committing.
Post - Call memberBoostPost or organizationBoostPost to create the sponsored campaign group, campaign, and creative that make up the boost.
Analytics - Call memberBoostAnalytics to retrieve performance metrics for member posts that have already been boosted.
Company Page Boost analytics aren't supported yet. It will be available in a future version. Use the Ad Analytics API for Company Page boost reporting.

Blocks.Text: The Boost button on the Page posts tab reflects the status returned by organizationBoostStatus. A disabled button indicates the post can't be boosted.

Selecting Boost opens the boost creation flow. Selecting a goal calls the init endpoint, changing the audience, budget, or schedule calls the hydrate endpoint to refresh the preview, and selecting Boost calls the post endpoint.
After a post is boosted, the Boost tab on the post analytics page shows the performance data returned by memberBoostAnalytics.
